paper_title: A Spectroscopic Search for Optical Emission Lines from Dark Matter Decay
coupling_convention: decay rate Gamma in s^-1 (NOT converted to g_agamma; y-axis of Fig. 8)
notes: Astrophysical search for ALP two-photon decay via stacked DESI dark-sky spectra around BGS/LRG galaxies (impact parameter ~50 kpc). The paper's main result (Fig. 8) is the two-photon decay rate Gamma [s^-1] vs particle mass m [eV] for m ~ 4-12 eV, from a 5-sigma line-flux limit of 1e-19 erg/s/cm^2/arcsec^2. The best bound corresponds to a lifetime > 3e25 s (Gamma < ~3.3e-26 s^-1). Values here are read approximately off the BGS 5-sigma curve and are given as DECAY RATE Gamma in s^-1, NOT as g_agamma; conversion to g_agamma requires Gamma = g^2 m^3/(64 pi) in natural units. Coupling type is ALP-photon. Not a haloscope, so no local DM density assumption; instead surface mass densities from weak lensing (~0.011 g/cm^2 for BGS, 0.021 g/cm^2 for LRG) were assumed. This is an astrophysical/telescope bound, so no DM density flag set.
